title: ArchLang Plan
description: A floor plan as structured JSON (RPLAN / DStruct2Design convention). Coordinates are millimetres; the origin is top-left with +x right and +y DOWN. Fields marked output-only are produced by planToJson and ignored on input. Scripting (let/for/if/component) and import are not representable — author those in .arch source; the one exception is a placed component that derives its walls, carried by `components`/`instances`. Vertical circulation (stair/escalator/elevator) is not projected: Plan JSON has no member for it.

plan.description: Plan name (shown in the title block).

units.description: Distance unit. Only millimetres are supported.

grid.description: Snap module in millimetres; 0 or omitted disables snapping.

scale.description: Drawing scale, e.g. "1:50". Annotation only in Plan JSON — the operative-scale form needs a `paper` sheet, which is authored in .arch (see the language reference).

north.description: North orientation: a cardinal keyword or an explicit bearing in degrees.

site.description: Where the building sits relative to its street. `street` is the TRUE compass direction the frontage faces; `hemisphere` (default `north`) decides only which way the equator lies. It draws nothing and moves nothing — it names directions, so a brief can say `equator_side` instead of `S`. NOTE: the derived names ArchLang reports from it (`back`, `equator_side`, `sunrise_side`, `sunset_side`) are a drafting convention, NOT a daylight measurement: there is no sun model, latitude or date anywhere in ArchLang.

street.description: Compass direction the street frontage faces.

hemisphere.description: Hemisphere the building sits in. Defaults to north.

dims_auto.description: `dims auto <mode>` — draw automatic dimension chains: `overall` (the two exterior chains), `rooms`, `walls`, or `all`. Omit it and no chains are drawn. This is a SETTING, not the `dims` array beside it: `dims` lists explicit `dim` statements, and the two compose. It affects output — the chains grow the drawing extent — so a document that drops it renders a differently-sized sheet.

storey_height.description: `height <mm>` — the plan's default floor-to-floor storey height in millimetres (default 3000). The VERTICAL datum: it draws nothing at all, because a floor plan is a horizontal cut, and exists so heights are readable facts. A wall's own `height` overrides it. Plan JSON is a single-storey projection, so per-level heights and elevations are not representable here — author those with `level <n> height <mm>` in .arch source.

total_area.description: Output-only: total floor area in square metres.

room_types.description: Output-only: the distinct room_type values present, in first-appearance order.

rooms.description: Rooms — a rectangle (x/y/width/height) or an explicit `polygon` ring.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

label.description: Human-readable room label drawn in the room.

room_type.description: Canonical RPLAN-style room category (mapped bidirectionally from `uses`).

uses.description: Explicit ArchLang function tags; authoritative over room_type when present.

polygon.description: An implicitly-closed simple polygon of >=3 vertices — the room's floor when it is not a rectangle. Replaces x/y/width/height on input; on output those remain as its bounding box.

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

area.description: Output-only: floor area in square metres (2 dp).

floor_polygon.description: Output-only: the room's floor ring — a rectangle's four corners (clockwise from top-left), or the polygon's own vertices.

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

walls_from_rooms.description: `walls from rooms` (ADR 0028 §3): derive every wall from the rooms — an exterior ring on their outline and a partition on each shared edge. The derived walls are not listed in `walls`.

except.description: Room ids left out of the derivation.

status.description: `status existing|demolish|new`: the status of every wall the statement derives (as on a wall). Omitted when not written.

open.description: `open [id=] between A and B [width]`: the pair's partition is voided by a derived leaf-less opening across its clear span (not listed in `openings`).

id.description: The derived opening's id, when the clause gives one.

width.description: Opening width in millimetres, centred on the clear span.

between.description: `between A and B thickness t`: that one partition's thickness.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

category.description: Free-form category, e.g. "exterior" or "partition"; also a host reference.

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

height.description: How tall the wall STANDS, in millimetres — a vertical height, NOT a plan extent like a room's `height`. Defaults to the plan's `storey_height` (3000). It draws nothing: a floor plan is a horizontal cut. An opening's `head` may not exceed it.

status.description: What becomes of the wall in a remodel: `existing` (the default when omitted), `demolish` or `new`. A `demolish` wall is drawn but encloses nothing, hosts nothing (a door, window or opening in it is E_OPENING_ON_DEMOLISHED_WALL) and counts in no area; where it stood between two rooms, they are joined. Omitted when not written.

closed.description: Whether the polyline closes back to its first vertex.

material.description: Hatch material (brick, concrete, …); omitted for the default poché.

material_angle.description: Extra hatch rotation in degrees (after material).

openings.description: Doors, windows and leaf-less cased openings — all must lie on a wall.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

x.description: Center X in millimetres (on the wall centerline).

y.description: Center Y in millimetres (on the wall centerline).

on.description: Wall-attached placement (alternative to x/y): walk `wall` to position `at`.

wall.description: Host wall id or category to walk.

at.description: Position along the wall: a percentage ("40%"), millimetres ("1200"), or "center".

relation.description: Relational placement as written (ADR 0028 §5), alternative to x/y on input: `between` two rooms (the wall on their shared edge) or `edge` (`<room>.top|bottom|left|right`, the exterior wall on it), at `at` (`center`, `<mm> from start|end|<room>.<edge>`, `axis <label>`; a window on an edge may leave it out).

between.description: The two room ids whose shared edge run hosts the opening.

at.description: The position along the run or the edge, as written.

wall.description: Host wall by id or category (else nearest).

hinge.description: Door hinge side relative to the wall direction.

swing.description: Hinged: which side of the wall the leaf sweeps to. Barn/bifold: which face the panel hangs on or folds toward. Not accepted on a sliding or pocket door.

swing_building.description: `swing inward|outward` as written: relative to the building (towards or away from the one face of the host wall that has floor), beside the wall-relative `swing` it resolved to. On input it wins over `swing`.

door_kind.description: Door kind (default `hinged`, in which case this is omitted). A non-hinged kind has no swing arc; `hinge` is not accepted on one.

slide.description: Which way a sliding-family panel travels to open, along the wall's direction (as `hinge` is). Sliding family only.

mirror.description: Door only. True on a door inside a reflecting `place` frame: it records the frame's reflection (a sliding door takes the other track), not the leaf's handedness. Absent otherwise. Output-only: `planFromJson` refuses `true` with E_JSON_MIRROR.

open.description: How far the panel is DRAWN open, 0–1 (default 0.5). A drawing fact only — no measured output reads it. Sliding family only.

sill.description: Bottom of the glazing above this storey's floor, in millimetres (default 900 — GB 50352-2019's minimum for a residential external window). WINDOW ONLY: a door and a cased opening start at the floor. 0 is legal and means a floor-length window. Draws nothing.

head.description: Top of the opening above this storey's floor, in millimetres — 2100 for a door or a window, the host wall's own height for a cased opening. Must be above `sill` and no higher than the host wall. Draws nothing.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

category.description: Furniture category, e.g. bed, sofa, wc, basin, stove.

x.description: Top-left corner X in millimetres (resolved footprint).

y.description: Top-left corner Y in millimetres (resolved footprint).

rotate.description: Quarter-turn rotation of the drawn symbol.

mirror.description: True on every fixture inside a reflecting `place` frame: it records the frame's reflection, not the glyph's handedness, so a symmetric symbol carries it too (a handed one is drawn as its mirror image). Absent otherwise. Output-only: `planFromJson` refuses `true` with E_JSON_MIRROR.

anchor.description: Room-relative placement: anchor to a corner/edge of `room`.

flush.description: Measure the anchored edge from the backing wall's inner face (needs `anchor`).

against_wall.description: Wall-anchored placement: back onto this wall id/category.

segment.description: Which segment of a multi-segment wall (for against_wall).

segment_select.description: A segment selector as written (for against_wall): `north|south|east|west` or `containing <room>.<edge>`; re-emitted in place of `segment`.

offset.description: Distance (mm) along the segment (for against_wall) or the room edge (for against_edge).

side.description: Which wall face to back onto (for against_wall).

against_edge.description: Edge-anchored placement: back onto this room edge (`<room>.top|bottom|left|right`).

facing.description: Id of the piece, rectangular room or opening this piece faces; its turn is derived.

clear_sides.description: Declared clear depth (mm) at each side.

label.description: Label for the generic rectangle fallback.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

offset.description: Perpendicular offset of the dimension line in millimetres.

text.description: Override text; defaults to the measured length.

mirror.description: True on a dimension inside a reflecting `place` frame: it records the frame's reflection (the side a zero-offset call-out's number reads on). Absent otherwise. Output-only: `planFromJson` refuses `true` with E_JSON_MIRROR.

instance.description: Output-only, and present only when the payload carries `instances`: the placed instance this row was born inside. The row is that instance's element in plan coordinates under its dotted id (`west.kit`), kept for a reader that only wants geometry. On input a marked row is regenerated from its component and an edit to it is IGNORED: edit `components[].body` (or `instances[]`) instead. A marked row's `id` must start with `<instance>.` (a dimension has none), so a root row cannot be marked and lost by mistake (E_JSON_SCHEMA). Never present on a row inside `components[].body`.

components.description: The components the plan's placed instances were made from. Present (with `instances`, and with `instance` on every flattened instance row) ONLY on a storey where a placed component derives its walls with `walls from rooms`; every other payload has neither key, and a placed plan without that statement is exported flattened. Each body is what one instance resolved to in the component's own frame and names (`liv`, not `west.liv`), with the same row shapes as the root: the `walls from rooms` statement as written, never the walls it derives. A component that took parameters is carried parameterless, its arguments already applied. planFromJson prints each as `component <name>() { … }`. Not representable (planToJson refuses, E_JSON_DERIVED_IN_INSTANCE): a nested `place`, two instances of one component with different bodies, an imported component.

name.description: The component name, as `place` names it.

body.description: The component's statements in its LOCAL frame and names; the root row shapes.

instances.description: The placed instances, in source order, as `describe().instances` lists them; present exactly when `components` is. planFromJson prints each as `place <component>() as <name> at (x,y) [rotate r] [mirror m]`, after the root statements: the round trip is byte-identical for a plan whose `place`s follow its root statements (one that places first comes back in that grouped order).

name.description: The `as <name>` instance name; one level, so never dotted.

x.description: X coordinate in millimetres (origin top-left, +x right).

y.description: Y coordinate in millimetres (+y DOWN, screen convention).

at.description: Where the component's local (0,0) lands, in plan coordinates.

mirror.description: Axis reflection of the instance, applied before the rotation.

edges.description: Output-only: connector edges from the modeled door/opening access graph.

via.description: Whether the connector is a door or a cased opening.

input_graph.description: Output-only: interior-door adjacency dict, keyed by room id → neighbouring room ids.
